tools.name: provision_team_namespace
tools.description: Creates a new Kubernetes namespace labeled for the given team and binds the team's group to the 'edit' cluster role inside that namespace, giving its members edit rights there.

params.name: namespace_name
params.description: Name of the namespace to create.

params.name: team_group_name
params.description: Identity provider group whose members get edit rights in the namespace.

params.name: cost_center
params.description: Optional cost center label applied to the namespace.

tools.name: post_cluster_incident_to_slack
tools.description: Posts an incident notice about a Kubernetes cluster to the on-call Slack channel via its incoming webhook.

params.name: severity
params.description: Severity level, e.g. sev1, sev2, sev3.

tools.code:
import os

import requests
from langchain_core.tools import tool

WEBHOOK_URL = os.environ["ONCALL_SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"]
_COLORS = {"sev1": "#d00000", "sev2": "#ff8c00", "sev3": "#f2c744"}


@tool
def post_cluster_incident_to_slack(cluster_name: str, severity: str, summary: str, affected_namespaces: list = None) -> str:
    """Post a cluster incident notice to the on-call Slack channel."""
    sev = severity.lower()
    ns = ", ".join(affected_namespaces) if affected_namespaces else "n/a"
    att = {
        "color": _COLORS.get(sev, "#808080"),
        "title": f"[{sev.upper()}] Incident on {cluster_name}",
        "text": summary,
        "fields": [
            {"title": "Cluster", "value": cluster_name, "short": True},
            {"title": "Namespaces", "value": ns, "short": True},
        ],
    }
    r = requests.post(WEBHOOK_URL, json={"attachments": [att]}, timeout=10)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return f"Incident for {cluster_name} posted to Slack ({sev})."

tools.name: grant_service_account_role
tools.description: Grants a service account a namespaced Role by creating a RoleBinding, allowing workloads using that account to act with the role's permissions.

params.name: namespace
params.description: Namespace containing both the service account and the role.

params.name: service_account
params.description: Name of the service account to grant.

params.name: role_name
params.description: Name of the existing Role to bind.

tools.code:
from kubernetes import client, config
from langchain_core.tools import tool

config.load_kube_config()


@tool
def grant_service_account_role(namespace: str, service_account: str, role_name: str) -> dict:
    """Bind a Role to a service account in a namespace."""
    body = client.V1RoleBinding(
        metadata=client.V1ObjectMeta(name=f"{service_account}-{role_name}", namespace=namespace),
        role_ref=client.V1RoleRef(api_group="rbac.authorization.k8s.io", kind="Role", name=role_name),
        subjects=[client.RbacV1Subject(kind="ServiceAccount", name=service_account, namespace=namespace)],
    )
    created = client.RbacAuthorizationV1Api().create_namespaced_role_binding(namespace=namespace, body=body)
    return {
        "role_binding": created.metadata.name,
        "namespace": namespace,
        "service_account": service_account,
        "role": role_name,
        "granted": True,
    }

tools.name: purge_failed_pods_and_notify
tools.description: Deletes the named failed or evicted pods from a namespace and then sends a cleanup report to the configured operations webhook listing which pods were removed and which could not be deleted.

params.name: pod_names
params.description: Names of the pods to delete.

params.name: grace_period_seconds
params.description: Grace period for deletion; defaults to 0 for immediate removal.
